units.title: Plant operator, all tickets, available (bump).
units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Bumping my post from earlier in the week. Still available for subcontract on the holm or anywhere else. CS30, CS31, CS38, own 13t excavator and forestry trailer, fully insured. Rang grieve again, very polite lady said the crew is 'fully resourced' again. Fully resourced twice now. Anyone else need a hand, tollinby to port ammet, no job too small.

units.title: Carrow Point readings, day 9.
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 07:00: 1016.2 hPa, wind southwest 4, air 9.0 C, dew point 4.1 C, visibility 35 km. I can see the Holm for the first time in five days, and Lisle church, and a tanker hull-down beyond. Fog total for the week by my station: 131 hours. Showers in the west today, says the Met Office. I say so too.

units.title: Garden waste: 'under one metre'.
units.author: sb_bins
units.text: The garden waste notice says branches must be cut to under one metre. The council's own tree on the Rope Walk verge has a branch two metres long hanging over the pavement at eye height, which I reported in August. I shall cut it to under one metre and leave it outside their office in a bag weighing no more than 20 kg. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.title: On time, day 9.
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: First on-time crossing in a week. The 06:40 arrived at 07:31, which is when it is supposed to arrive, and the whole saloon looked at each other in mild disbelief. Somebody clapped. The coffee machine, sensing an opportunity to keep us humble, broke.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Thank you, skipper. So night 7 has all the signs of a person: movement, a slip on the weed, a direction of travel up into the village. That's one explained, or nearly. Night 4 remains open, and I don't think there is anything wrong with leaving it open until somebody knows more. Open is not the same as mysterious.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Day three of asking and still nobody can tell me why it has to be every tree in thirty days. Not some. All. You don't clear an island like that for a hotel; guests want trees. You clear it so you can see across it. I'm just asking what anybody would want to see coming.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Gil, 'Not some. All.' is not, strictly, a sentence, though I grant it is effective. As to your question, my late husband cleared a whole field of gorse once in a fortnight, and when I asked him why all of it, he said 'because it was cheaper than doing it twice'. Mrs Hale (retd.)

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Every tree in thirty days because the contract says thirty days, the price is per tree and winter is coming. Clear-felling is cheaper per tree than selective felling, and a fast job is a cheaper job. None of that needs a reason beyond money. What would we expect if it were something else? Some trace of the something else.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Bernard, please don't. Report it again through the council's highways page and post the reference number here, and I will raise it on the next liaison call with the officer. I have been on the receiving end of a bag of branches before and it did not speed anything up. Pell, admin.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding 4: Ardent Vale has filed nothing new in the company registry this month: no new charges, no change of directors, no new subsidiaries. I check weekly. That is a non-finding, I know, but non-findings are findings too, and I said I would report what I found, whatever it was.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Evening crossing, also on time, I'm almost unsettled. For the slipway thread people, since it came up: Kerris told me on the boat this morning she'd rather night 4 stayed open than got closed wrong. She is the most level-headed person on that ferry, the engine included.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Brackwater junction: four minutes, but in sunshine, which somehow makes it worse. The pasty man has a colleague now and they are both looking into the hole. Gordon the cone is back on our side. Progress report ends. Home by seven for once.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 19:30 readings: 1014.0 hPa and falling, wind southwest 5, gusting 28 knots on the mast. One shower at 15:20, 1.4 mm. Clear between. Lamps lit along the Gilliver shore across the water, as usual. A good day for the station after a week of staring at my own gate.

units.title: Pebble update, day 9
units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Pebble update: still away. Mr Arkle held the ladder (thank you, TollinbyMum, he did) and I checked every garage roof behind Tanners Lane. Found a tennis ball, a child's shoe and a very surprised pigeon. Biscuit box again tonight. Grey, one white sock, green collar with a bell she hates.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: To add one thing to Ferrous. A consent for total clearance usually means the owner intends to replant, sell, or apply for something later. All three are common. It is on the record that they have done none of them yet. 'Not yet' is not a conspiracy. It is how most planning files look for years.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Davey, you'd not want it. A month on a rock with no pub and a boat that leaves at dusk whether you're on it or not. Take the hedges in Tollinby. Hedges don't care what the weather's doing and you sleep in your own bed. Aye, I mean it kindly.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: One thought: if she has been in somewhere tight, the bell may have been pulled off the collar. Do ask neighbours to listen for her voice rather than the bell, especially early in the morning when it's quiet. Pell

units.title: Power off in east Tollinby?
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Power just went at ours in east Tollinby, about ten to eight, with a bang off toward Brackwater. The kids think it's an adventure. I think the freezer has two weeks of batch cooking in it and I am not doing that again. Anyone know anything? Sound FM says the substation.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: The whole of Brackwater is dark. Saw a blue flash over the substation from the cottage, then the bang. The water lads already have a generator going at the pumping station; you can hear it across the reservoir. Stay off the reservoir road tonight. There's a police car at the junction and no lights anywhere.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Ha, no pub is a dealbreaker Bram, I'll think on it. Hedges dont pay a hundred a tree though. Then again hedges dont need a boat. Then again again my van needs a new clutch. Ill keep the post up a few more days and see who rings.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: On my way to Brackwater with the crew now. Can't say anything about cause, and wouldn't if I could, Garvey would have me. If your power is off, switch off big appliances so they don't all come back on at once, and leave one light switched on so you know when we've done it.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Thank you, Mr Pell, I hadn't thought of the bell. Power is off at my sister's in Tollinby so she's coming to stay tonight, which means two of us shaking the biscuit box at the back door. Pebble would hate this. Pebble would come home just to tell us off.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: We're on it. It's at the substation, not your house and not your line. We're switching you back from the Tollinby side in stages. Don't ring the faults line to ask what happened, we don't know yet; ring it if you've got a line down. I'll say what it was when I know and not before.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: a hundred a tree and you're still asking on a forum. tells you everything about how much they want you, mate. sell the excavator and buy a car off me.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: squirrel. it's always a squirrel. they find the one bit in the whole place that goes bang and they sit on it.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Back on at 21:55 at ours. Freezer survived, the kids are furious it's over and want to know when the next one is. Thank you to the line crews out there tonight. Garvey, if it was a squirrel, I would like to know, and so would my youngest, who has drawn it.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: A substation goes bang in the same week someone circulates a notice about evacuation sites. I'm not saying sabotage. I'm saying nobody official has said it isn't. The co-op asked people 'not to speculate'. Why would you need to ask that?

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: you lot are still on about this?? the slip is a slip. someone stood on it, someone else stood on it, the end. go to bed. some of us have college

units.author: hollow_signal

edit.text: Strange night... the lights are telling us something. It starts with the substations. Watch the coast next. Remember who said it first.

units.text: Strange night... the lights are telling us something. Watch them. I won't say more on an open board, but some of us aren't surprised.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Still dark in the lane behind the bookshop at two, though the main street came back an hour ago. Reading by candle, which is how most of my stock was meant to be read. Somewhere over toward Brackwater a generator is holding one long note, like an organ someone has leaned on.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Drove home early from the retail park through the Brackwater junction around half one. Signals dead, one police car with its blues going doing the job by hand, a long queue of very polite drivers. The van I keep mentioning on Lamp Hours was not at the junction. Saying so only because somebody will ask.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Science or not, son, tonight there is no power in the village, a generator at the pumping station and a police car at the junction. Anybody I find in the woods after dark tonight I will be walking back to their car personally. That includes the polite one with the dish.

units.title: fog gone, boats out
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: fog gone lads. half the harbour out before six. queue at the diesel pump at 05:40, told you it would be. chandlery has crab bands back in stock and you'll need them, by the sound of what's coming up in the pots

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you all for staying in during the fog; it was the right call every day. Normal working resumes. The Lisle South buoy is being repaired this morning. Spring tides: please mind the bottom of the slip at low water today, around 12:35. Thank you.

units.title: Kevin
units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Morning crossing note: a heron was standing on the bow rail when we came alongside at Gilliver at 07:05, and refused to leave until Finn waved a mop at it. Finn has named it Kevin and is claiming vindication. I make no comment. The new floodlight lamp is working well, which is how we saw Kevin.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: diesel up another cent from the supplier today. I know. I know. Bram you can complain to my face when you fill up, you did this morning already so you're ahead

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: kevin is a legend and I said heron from the start, I'm not saying kevin was on the slip on night 4, I'm saying kevin has form and kevin was on the boat, which is closer to the slip than any of you lot have been

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Kevin is about a metre tall with his neck out, Finn. I'm very pleased for Kevin. Night 4 was not Kevin. I'll leave it there, and you can leave Kevin on the rail next time; he wasn't hurting anybody.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: kevin is banned from the chandlery roof, he has been for years, he just doesn't read the notices. pass it on

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Lifted forty pots. Half the crabs clawless, as we said. Lobsters fine, the clever beggars. Price at the merchant's will be poor tomorrow. Holm side was flat calm under the cliff and lumpy off the point, wind against tide. Glad to be out, though. Five days ashore is enough to make a man paint things.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: lights out at brackwater apparently, gilliver fine. chandlery open at 7 tomorrow as usual. torches and batteries on the counter if anyone's got family over that side

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Lights stayed on here, we're on the other feeder. You could see the dark patch over Brackwater way from the harbour wall, like somebody had put a hand over that part of the hills. Lamps lit in the windows here same as always, power or no power.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: leave kevin alone hes been through enough this week. also hes taller than finn when he stretches, i've seen him on the chippy bins

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Quay Road pole changed this afternoon, I climbed it, Garvey was right about the stay, I could feel the wires pulling when the new one went up. Gloves were good. Off home for a bath, unless the phone goes. Which it will, because it's me.
